description: Rename every crate that is a Rust translation/fork of an externally-trademarked open-source project to carry the outram-park-fork- prefix, so the name is unmistakably a fork and not the official project (see TRADEMARKS.md). Per-crate rename scope: (1) package name in the crate's Cargo.toml, (2) directory under crates/, (3) [workspace] members path in root Cargo.toml, (4) every path dependency on it in other crates' Cargo.toml, (5) every 'use <old_crate>::' / extern references in dependent crates + examples + tests, (6) publish metadata/README/docs mentions, (7) any CI / scripts referencing the path. crate:: self-references do NOT change (package-internal). Do the renames one crate at a time, leaning on the compiler as the reference checker (per CLAUDE.md). Book-keeping only for now — do not execute.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
New external-project forks (e.g. outram-park-fork-coolprop, op-kbc) are born with the outram-park-fork- prefix -- they need no rename, only the existing crates in this epic's children do.
Naming exception (user, 2026-07-10): the three OpenFOAM-derived crates (op-ahi.1/.2/.3) now target an outram-foam- prefix instead of this epic's general outram-park-fork- prefix — user's explicit call, not derived from the original epic rationale. njoy/openmc/dwsim (op-ahi.4/.5/.6) are unaffected and keep the outram-park-fork- prefix. Each OpenFOAM rename must also add an explicit README/docs disambiguation note ("OUTRAM PARK's Rust fork of OpenFOAM, not the official ESI/OpenCFD OpenFOAM(R) software") and reconcile TRADEMARKS.md, which currently names a third, now-stale spelling (outram-park-openfoam-fork-*).
Correction 2026-07-13: the 2026-07-10 note above said njoy/openmc/dwsim (op-ahi.4/.5/.6) were unaffected by the outram-foam- exception -- that was wrong for openmc. User extended the same naming exception to it: op-ahi.4 is now closed as outram-mc-libs (not outram-park-fork-openmc-libs). njoy (op-ahi.5) and dwsim (op-ahi.6) remain unconfirmed either way -- do not assume they're exceptions too without asking; only openfoam and openmc have been explicitly named by the user so far. op-ahi.1/.2/.3/.4 are all done and closed as of 2026-07-13; only op-ahi.5 (njoy) and op-ahi.6 (dwsim) remain open in this epic.

title: Trademark-compliance crate renames: outram-park-fork-<project> prefix

description:
Parent: op-841p. Meshing sits UPSTREAM of rung 3 - GeN-Foam cannot run without a mesh - so it is part of the pipeline, not beside it.

MAINTAINER DECISIONS: (1) CLI tools first, not a GUI. (2) ONE tet-dual mesh used for BOTH neutronics and thermal hydraulics, not two. (3) GUI later via op-hzs.53.

START FROM WHAT EXISTS (verified 2026-08-11):
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/pipeline.rs:312 surface_to_tet_dual_mesh(points, tris, opts) -> Result<(VolumeMesh, TetDualReport), String>. IMPLEMENTED, body is run_pipeline at :392. Seven stages (carve, snap, tetrahedralize, Delaunay flip, dual, Laplacian smooth, boundary layers), each optional stage gated by acceptable() at :243 with graceful fallback via keep_if_ok at :253. TetDualReport at :217 already carries max_non_orthogonality_deg, max_skewness, n_negative_volume_cells. Multipatch variant at :379 with a documented limitation at :346-353 (boundary layers grow on the whole boundary, not per patch).
- Quality metrics implemented at crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/checks.rs:78 (check_quality): non-orthogonality :95-97, skewness :99-106, aspect ratio :130, OpenFOAM thresholds in is_good() at :70.
- CLI tools that generate or convert a mesh TODAY: blockMesh, ideasUnvToFoam, polyDualMesh in crates/outram-foam-cli/src/bin/. outram-foam-mesh has NO binaries - it is a pure library (block_mesh.rs:490, snappy_hex_mesh.rs:186, poly_dual_mesh.rs:779, driver.rs:345 mesh_from_surface with write_case at :306, mesh_quality.rs:274 assess_quality).

INPUTS: HTR-10 core geometry - 180 cm diameter, 197 cm average height, 100 cm side reflector including carbon bricks, the conus and discharge tube, plus 10 control-rod borings (13 cm at r = 102.1 cm), 7 absorber-ball, 3 irradiation, and 20 helium channels (8 cm at r = 144.6 cm). CAUTION: the axial build is NOT fully specified in the open text - see the geometry bead.

OUTPUTS: a polyMesh consumed by GeN-Foam, plus a quality report. Non-orthogonality and skewness MUST be measured and reported, and the mesh plus its generation parameters go in the run manifest - a result on an unrecorded mesh is not reproducible.

WHY ONE MESH: it avoids cross-mesh mapping error at the coupling seam. op-p6p.8 (genfoam multiRegion cross-mesh coupling) exists precisely for the case where meshes DO differ, so the shared-mesh choice is a deliberate simplification that sidesteps it. OPEN QUESTION for the maintainer: neutronics wants resolution at the core/reflector interface and rod channels, TH wants it at the near-wall porosity rise and the axial thermal gradient. On a shared mesh the union must be resolved, which costs cells the coarser physics does not need.
title: HTR-10 meshing: tet-dual polyMesh of the core, shared by neutronics and TH, with a measured quality report

description:
Maintainer decision 2026-08-12: replace the single lumped bed control volume with a genuine unstructured TETRAHEDRAL mesh of 15-25 cells.

RATIONALE (maintainer, and it is the deciding one): this is a stepping stone to COARSE-MESH GEN-FOAM AND NODAL METHODS on this geometry. The tet cells are not chosen for rendering or for accuracy at 20 cells -- they are the data structure the FV/nodal machinery will need. Judged against 'is 20 tets an accurate bed' this looks over-engineered; judged against 'does this give GeN-Foam something to stand on' it is the right call.

This retires an earlier caveat I recorded: I flagged that KTA and ZBS have no published face-based tet formulation and would have to be derived. That is too strong for the target approach -- GeN-Foam's POROUS-MEDIUM formulation applies 1-D friction closures like KTA as per-cell momentum sink terms, which is standard practice, not an invention. Maintainer confirmed KTA and ZBS are fine to carry over.

COST IS NOT THE ISSUE: ~20 zone balances at the 10 Hz timestep is ~200 zone-updates/s on a thermal-hydraulics thread currently at 20% duty. The GUI is doing ~600000 circle tessellations/s by comparison (op-szmi.12). Tet physics is roughly 3000x cheaper than what the renderer already does, and lands on a different thread.

SEQUENCING: do this AFTER op-szmi.12 (the pebble-bed texture bake), because the bake's per-vertex tint seam is being built specifically so an axially/spatially varying bed can be painted as a handful of quads with interpolated vertex colours rather than 10000 recoloured circles. Landing the mesh first would mean painting per-zone colour through the slow path.

MUST NOT REGRESS: the honesty contracts. A resolved mesh removes the 'one control volume' caveat but NOT the others -- still no momentum equation feeding pressure drop back on flow, still no natural circulation, unless those are actually implemented. Update the contracts to what is true after the change, neither over- nor under-stating.
title: htgr_sim_v1: nodalise the pebble bed onto 15-25 tet cells

description: Two honest remainders from op-u6s.4 GPU wire-in (2026-07-17): (a) UnionTotalXs is a dense LOG-SPACED resample of macro_xs_total, not a union of the constituent nuclides' native ENDF energy breakpoints -- narrow resonances between log nodes are smeared; build the true native-breakpoint union. (b) run_keff_gpu only uses the GPU for the per-generation FIRST-FLIGHT Sigma_t batch; the branchy per-collision walk stays on CPU. Investigate an event-based/Woodcock collision-site batch so more of the sweep's XS lookups go through the GPU (or document that history-based transport fundamentally caps GPU penetration here).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-desktop-aftershock
notes.content: Deep GPU penetration pass delivered (worktree, 2026-07-17). DONE: (a) native-breakpoint union grid — Nuclide::native_energy_grid + UnionTotalXs::tabulate_native (10834 nodes on Godiva, ~2.7x more accurate than equal-size dense-log). (b) event-based batched-flight GPU kernel — a batch of live neutrons stays resident in GPU buffers; per dispatch the GPU does RNG(emulated 64-bit LCG, bit-exact state) + native-union Sigma_t binary-search + d_col sample + sphere flight + leak test for the WHOLE batch; only branchy collision physics stays on CPU. Wired under ComputeType::Gpu (run_keff_gpu_batched), CPU fallback + Android gating intact. k agreement: GPU within 0.16 sigma of single-thread reference. RNG decision: per-history LCG streams, GPU state advance bit-exact, f32 flight -> reproducible run-to-run but NOT bit-identical to single-thread; CPU single stays trusted reference. HONEST TIMING VERDICT: GPU loses to CpuMultiThread at ALL batch sizes 1e3..1e6, NO crossover (1e6: multi ~3-7s vs GPU ~19-34s). Cause: memory-transfer/launch bound — event loop round-trips CPU/GPU boundary once per event because collision physics is on CPU. NOT closing (GPU did not win anywhere). Tests: 80->90 lib tests pass, Android clean. See docs/ai-fleet-review/gpu-deep-transport/REVIEW_MANIFEST.md + verification_and_validation/gpu_batched_transport/README.md.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
NOT WORKED in the 2026-08-11 HTR-10-focused session; recorded so the skip is visible.

Both halves of this bead are already delivered per the 2026-07-17 comment (native-breakpoint union grid, and the event-based batched-flight kernel), and what keeps it open is the honest timing verdict: GPU loses to CpuMultiThread at every batch size 1e3..1e6 with no crossover, because the event loop round-trips the CPU/GPU boundary once per event. That is an optimisation question, not an HTR-10 blocker - HTR-10 rung 1 (op-jv1s) needs a CORRECT pebble-bed k_eff with graphite S(alpha,beta), not a faster one, and correctness there is blocked on op-hc2o rather than on GPU penetration.

Useful datum for whoever picks this up: this host DOES have a usable adapter (NVIDIA RTX 3050, Vulkan, discrete, 12 CPU threads - see the op-9s8.2 comment of the same date for the full probe output), so the crossover measurement CAN be re-taken here on real hardware rather than inferred. Every GPU-vs-CPU-mirror test in the crate ran green on it this session.

title: outram-mc: native-breakpoint union grid + deeper GPU penetration in run_keff_gpu
